findings.text: blocking: the assertion `"read_iron_core" in names or "read_west_iron_outline" in names` is satisfied by the code path that already existed at base 0c74ef1 — all twelve WEST_READERS contain `read_iron_core` and none contains a FLAT_OUTLINE_NAMES token at that revision — so it cannot fail on a regression of this read and no production file calls `read_west_iron_outline` at 69387540c; the done_when clause that the script readers call this read is therefore both unmet and unmeasured, and the repair (point one scoped reader at the new read, require that name in the test) lies inside the node's own write paths.

non-blocking: `IronFillRegion.covered` re-implements the point-in-polygon mask the repository owns at nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:70 (`inside_polygon`, public in `__all__`, numpy, no shapely) and nova/imas/machine.py already imports from that module at line 21; it duplicates rather than wraps the owner, so a cell counted inside here and inside a vessel mask can drift apart with no test to notice.

non-blocking: a second flat-outline construction (`west_regions`, `flat_fill`, `WEST_JOIN` at lines 291-335) remains in the tree with its consumer scripts/iron_limb_production/measure.py:252, so the done_when's "no second construction of the flat outline in the tree" is unmet; both paths lie outside this node's write paths and the node correctly recorded them under outside_scope rather than editing them.

non-blocking: `IronCoreOutline.cross_field` — with `IronCoreOutline.fill` at line 640 and `IronFillRegion.covered` — is public surface added without any assertion (tests exercise only `cross_field_factor`), and the per-cell demagnetising factor is not a fill fraction, so it is both untested and beyond the goal.
